title: 366. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Volume of Cylinders
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the volume of a cylinder using its radius and height.
questions.question: A right circular cylinder has radius \(2\text{ cm}\) and height \(5\text{ cm}\). What is its volume?
questions.explanation:
Use the volume formula for a cylinder:
\[
V=\pi r^2h.
\]
Substitute \(r=2\) and \(h=5\):
\[
V=\pi(2)^2(5)=\pi(4)(5)=20\pi\text{ cm}^3.
\]
So the volume is \(20\pi\text{ cm}^3\).
questions.hint: Use the formula \(V=\pi r^2h\) and square the radius before multiplying by the height.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the volume formula \(V=\pi r^2h\) to find the volume of a cylinder.
questions.question: A cylinder has radius \(3\text{ cm}\) and height \(4\text{ cm}\). What is its volume?
questions.explanation:
Using \(V=\pi r^2h\), substitute \(r=3\) and \(h=4\):
\[
V=\pi(3)^2(4)=\pi(9)(4)=36\pi\text{ cm}^3.
\]
Therefore, the volume is \(36\pi\text{ cm}^3\).
questions.hint: Square the radius first, then multiply by the height and by \(\pi\).

questions.concept: Volume of a Cylinder from Diameter
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the volume of a cylinder given its diameter and height.
questions.question: A cylinder has diameter \(10\text{ cm}\) and height \(6\text{ cm}\). What is its volume?
questions.explanation:
The radius is half the diameter:
\[
r=\frac{10}{2}=5\text{ cm}.
\]
Now use \(V=\pi r^2h\):
\[
V=\pi(5)^2(6)=\pi(25)(6)=150\pi\text{ cm}^3.
\]
So the volume is \(150\pi\text{ cm}^3\).
questions.hint: First find the radius from the diameter, then use the cylinder volume formula.

questions.concept: Volume of a Cylinder from Base Area
questions.learningObjective: Determine the volume of a cylinder from its base area and height.
questions.question: A cylinder has base area \(12\text{ cm}^2\) and height \(9\text{ cm}\). What is its volume?
questions.explanation:
For a cylinder, the volume equals the base area multiplied by the height:
\[
V=Bh.
\]
Substitute \(B=12\) and \(h=9\):
\[
V=12\times9=108\text{ cm}^3.
\]
Therefore, the volume is \(108\text{ cm}^3\).
questions.hint: When the base area is given, use \(V=Bh\) instead of calculating \(\pi r^2\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the height of a cylinder from its volume and radius.
questions.question: A cylinder has volume \(100\pi\text{ cm}^3\) and radius \(5\text{ cm}\). What is its height?
questions.explanation:
Use \(V=\pi r^2h\). Substitute \(V=100\pi\) and \(r=5\):
\[
100\pi=\pi(5)^2h=25\pi h.
\]
Divide both sides by \(25\pi\):
\[
h=\frac{100\pi}{25\pi}=4\text{ cm}.
\]
So the height is \(4\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Substitute the known values into \(V=\pi r^2h\), then solve for \(h\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the radius of a cylinder from its volume and height.
questions.question: A cylinder has volume \(72\pi\text{ cm}^3\) and height \(8\text{ cm}\). What is its radius?
questions.explanation:
Using \(V=\pi r^2h\), substitute \(V=72\pi\) and \(h=8\):
\[
72\pi=\pi r^2(8)=8\pi r^2.
\]
Divide both sides by \(8\pi\):
\[
r^2=9.
\]
Since the radius must be positive,
\[
r=3\text{ cm}.
\]
questions.hint: Solve \(V=\pi r^2h\) for \(r^2\), then take the positive square root.

questions.learningObjective: Compare the volumes of two cylinders using the volume formula.
questions.question: Cylinder A has radius \(4\text{ cm}\) and height \(5\text{ cm}\). Cylinder B has radius \(5\text{ cm}\) and height \(4\text{ cm}\). Which cylinder has the greater volume?
questions.explanation:
For Cylinder A:
\[
V_A=\pi(4)^2(5)=80\pi\text{ cm}^3.
\]
For Cylinder B:
\[
V_B=\pi(5)^2(4)=100\pi\text{ cm}^3.
\]
Since \(100\pi>80\pi\), Cylinder B has the greater volume.
questions.hint: Calculate the volume of each cylinder separately using \(V=\pi r^2h\), then compare them.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the volume of a cylindrical container in a practical context.
questions.question: A cylindrical water tank has radius \(2\text{ m}\) and height \(3\text{ m}\). What is its volume?
questions.explanation:
Use the cylinder volume formula:
\[
V=\pi r^2h.
\]
Substitute \(r=2\) and \(h=3\):
\[
V=\pi(2)^2(3)=\pi(4)(3)=12\pi\text{ m}^3.
\]
So the volume of the tank is \(12\pi\text{ m}^3\).
questions.hint: Use the radius and height in \(V=\pi r^2h\), and keep the units in cubic meters.

questions.concept: Volume of Liquid in a Cylinder
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the volume of liquid in a partially filled cylinder.
questions.question: A cylindrical container has radius \(6\text{ cm}\) and height \(15\text{ cm}\). It is filled with water to \(\frac{2}{3}\) of its height. What is the volume of the water?
questions.explanation:
The water forms a cylinder with radius \(6\text{ cm}\) and height
\[
\frac{2}{3}\times15=10\text{ cm}.
\]
Its volume is
\[
V=\pi(6)^2(10)=\pi(36)(10)=360\pi\text{ cm}^3.
\]
Therefore, the volume of the water is \(360\pi\text{ cm}^3\).
questions.hint: Find the height of the water first, then use the cylinder volume formula with the same radius.

questions.concept: Volume Conservation in Recasting a Cylinder
questions.learningObjective: Solve a volume-conservation problem when a cylinder is recast into another cylinder.
questions.question: A solid cylinder has radius \(3\text{ cm}\) and height \(8\text{ cm}\). It is melted and recast into another cylinder with radius \(2\text{ cm}\). What is the height of the new cylinder?
questions.explanation:
The volume of the original cylinder is
\[
V=\pi(3)^2(8)=\pi(9)(8)=72\pi\text{ cm}^3.
\]
Recasting conserves volume, so the new cylinder also has volume \(72\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Let its height be \(h\). Then
\[
72\pi=\pi(2)^2h=4\pi h.
\]
Divide both sides by \(4\pi\):
\[
h=18\text{ cm}.
\]
Thus, the height of the new cylinder is \(18\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: The volume stays the same after recasting. Use \(V=\pi r^2h\) for both cylinders and equate their volumes.
